summary: Tested the new Token Generator feature (POST /api/generate_token) and the Tokens screen. Backend: 12/12 pytest cases passed covering all 6 token types (bearer, password, uuid, totp, otp, session), ledger integration (context prefixed with 'token:', strictly increasing block_id), and 422 validation for invalid type. Regression on /api/status and /api/get_random still passes. Frontend: 5-tab bottom nav confirmed, Tokens screen renders, type chips switch config panels & description correctly, generation works for bearer/uuid/totp/password (with toggles honoured — lower-only produced [a-z]+), token-output/token-value/token-health/token-block-id all render, TOTP produces base64 QR image, history panel shows items in descending block_id order and clear-history-btn empties it.

minor.issue: The `length` field is interpreted as INPUT byte count then base64url-encoded, so passing length=43 (frontend default) produces a 58-char token. If the intent (per review request) is 'token of expected length', either the parameter should mean output-char length or docs/frontend should be updated. Currently the character set is correct ([A-Za-z0-9-_]) and length is deterministic (~4/3 of input), just not equal to the requested value.

ui_bugs.issue: navigator.clipboard.writeText().then(...) has no .catch — in headless / restricted-permission browsers this becomes an unhandled promise rejection which the webpack-dev-server error overlay surfaces as a full-page 'Uncaught runtime errors' modal that blocks all further interaction. Add a .catch(() => setCopied(true)) or a try/catch fallback (execCommand or silently ignore).

action_items: Add .catch on navigator.clipboard.writeText() in TokensScreen.copyToken to avoid unhandled promise rejection when clipboard permission is denied.
Clarify the semantics of `length` for type=session: either return exactly N base64url chars, or update the frontend default (43) and hint text so users know they get ceil(N*4/3) chars.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew to ~690 lines; consider splitting token helpers (BASE62/BASE32/_to_charset/_uuid4_from_entropy/_base32_secret/_base64url) into a tokens.py module for maintainability.
_to_charset uses `stream[i] % n` — for alphabets not a divisor of 256 there is minor modulo bias (documented in comment but worth noting for the base62 case in bearer/password).

TOTP otpauth URI does not URL-encode the issuer or label — 'ChaosKey+' contains '+' which some authenticator apps interpret as a space. Recommend urllib.parse.quote for label & issuer segments and query values.
TokenRequest allows prefix up to arbitrary length; server truncates to 32 in ctx but not in output token. Consider server-side prefix length cap for consistency with frontend's 24-char slice.
No rate limit on /api/generate_token — every call writes a ledger block; a client could grow the ledger unbounded. Consider soft throttle.

success_rate.frontend: 100% functional (1 medium UX bug: clipboard catch)

seed_data_creation: Test run appended ~15-20 signed ledger blocks (token: contexts + regression get_random).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Tokens feature is fully functional. Backend pytest at /app/backend/tests/test_tokens.py (12 tests). Frontend Tokens tab is index 1 in 5-tab bottom nav. Clipboard writeText will throw NotAllowedError in headless — either avoid clicking copy-token-btn or expect a webpack error overlay unless the .catch fix ships. TOTP QR is generated client-side by the `qrcode` library (data:image/png;base64,...). Session token length is a known ambiguity — see minor backend issue.
rca of the issue: Clipboard overlay bug: navigator.clipboard.writeText is a Promise that rejects in insecure or permission-denied contexts (headless). TokensScreen.copyToken chains only .then and no .catch, so the rejection bubbles up. CRA/webpack-dev-server surfaces unhandled promise rejections as a full-viewport error overlay in dev mode, which intercepts pointer events. Fix: add .catch to the promise (e.g. navigator.clipboard.writeText(...).then(...).catch(() => {})) or wrap in try/catch with a document.execCommand('copy') fallback.
